{{nihongo|'''Kokuwakura Shrine Haiden'''|子鍬倉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

'''Kokuwakura Shrine''' (こくわくらじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Agedo, {{ill|Taira|ja|平 (いわき市)|qid=Q128846894|lt=Taira}}, {{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|ar|لواكي (فوكوشيما)|arz|لواكى|azb|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|bg|Иваки|ca|Iwaki|ce|Иваки (Фукусима)|ceb|Iwaki-shi|de|Iwaki|eo|Iwaki|es|Iwaki (Fukushima)|eu|Iwaki (Fukushima)|fa|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|fi|Iwaki|fr|Iwaki|ga|Iwaki|gl|Iwaki|hu|Ivaki (Fukusima)|hy|Իվակի|id|Iwaki, Fukushima|is|Iwaki|it|Iwaki|ja|いわき市|kk|Иваки|ko|이와키시|lt|Ivakis|mg|Iwaki|mzn|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|nl|Iwaki (Fukushima)|no|Iwaki|pl|Iwaki|pt|Iwaki|ro|Iwaki|ru|Иваки (город)|sh|Ivaki|simple|Iwaki, Fukushima|sr|Иваки|sv|Iwaki|tg|Иваки|th|อิวากิ (จังหวัดฟูกูชิมะ)|tl|Iwaki, Fukushima|tr|Iwaki, Fukuşima|tt|Иваки (Фукусима)|uk|Івакі (Фукусіма)|ur|ایواکی، فوکوشیما|uz|Ivaki(Iwaki), Fukushima|vi|Iwaki, Fukushima|war|Iwaki, Fukushima|za|Banjsingz Si|zh|磐城市|zh_classical|磐城市|zh_min_nan|Iwaki-chhī|zh_yue|磐城|qid=Q274384}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha (minor shrine)}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was designated a prefectural shrine.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the first year of {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} ({{ill|806|ab|806|af|806|als|806|am|806 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|806|ar|806|ary|806|ast|806|az|806|azb|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|bar|806|bcl|806|be|806|be_x_old|806|bg|806|bn|৮০৬|bpy|মারি ৮০৬|br|806|bs|806.|ca|806|cdo|806 nièng|ceb|806|ckb|٨٠٦|crh|806|cs|806|csb|806|cv|806|cy|806|da|806|de|806|el|806|eml|806|eo|806|es|806|et|806|eu|806|fa|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|fi|806|fo|806|fr|806|frr|806|fy|806|ga|806|gan|806年|gd|806|gl|806|he|806|hi|806|hr|806.|ht|806 (almanak jilyen)|hu|806|hy|806|id|806|ilo|806|io|806|is|806|it|806|ja|806年|jv|806|ka|806|kaa|806|kk|806 жыл|ko|806년|la|806|lb|806|lij|806|lmo|806|lt|806 m.|lv|806. gads|map_bms|806|mdf|806|mg|806|mhr|806|mk|806|mr|इ.स. ८०६|mrj|806 и|ms|806|mzn|۸۰۶|nah|806|nap|806|nds|806|new|सन् ८०६|nl|806|nn|806|no|806|nrm|806|nso|806|oc|806|or|୮୦୬|os|806-æм аз|pl|806|pt|806|qu|806|ro|806|ru|806 год|rue|806|sa|८०६|scn|806|sd|806ع|se|806|sh|806.|shn|806|si|806|sk|806|sl|806|smn|806|sq|806|sr|806|su|806|sv|806|sw|806|tg|Соли 806|th|พ.ศ. 1349|tk|806|tl|806|tly|806|tr|806|tt|806 ел|uk|806|ur|806ء|uz|806|vec|806|vi|806|vls|806|war|806|wuu|806年|xmf|806|zh|806年|zh_min_nan|806 nî|zh_yue|806年|qid=Q30021}}). It is an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}} and one of the seven Shikinaisha of Iwaki Province. In ancient times it was said to be the general guardian shrine of the four districts of Iwaki ({{ill|Kikuta district|ja|菊多郡|qid=Q11619613}}, {{ill|Iwaki district|ja|磐城郡|qid=Q11587876}}, {{ill|Iwasaki district|ja|磐前郡|qid=Q11587858}}, and {{ill|Naraha district|Q11541347|qid=Q11541347}}).

As one of the “Three Shrines of Taira Castle,” deities protecting {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Taira Castle}}, it was venerated by successive lords of the castle.

In {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 6 ({{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}}), construction of {{ill|Iwakitaira Castle|Q11587869|qid=Q11587869}} reduced the shrine’s land, leading to its decline. However, in {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 9 ({{ill|1826|Q7004|qid=Q7004}}), the fourth lord of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Taira Domain}}, {{ill|Naitō Yoshimune|Q8514975|qid=Q8514975}}, restored a small {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inari}} shrine that had stood in Sakuramachi and relocated it to the present site.

In March of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was elevated to the rank of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. Even after the abolition of the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 21, it continued to be affectionately called “Kensha” (prefectural shrine).

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 7, the {{ill|Escarpment|Q1174791|qid=Q1174791}} on the southern front was cut away to create the “Men’s Slope,” and in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 10 the “Women’s Slope” was completed.

=== Shrine Name ===
“{{ill|Ko|Q1307938|qid=Q1307938}}” is said to mean “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=silkworm}},” symbolizing “clothing”; the agricultural tool “{{ill|Hoe (tool)|Q131154|qid=Q131154}}” represents “food”; and “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kura (storehouse)}}” represents “shelter.” Together, the name is said to express the divine virtues of the enshrined deity governing “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=clothing, food, and shelter}}.”

=== Shrine Buildings ===
In April of {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 2, a fire destroyed the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine buildings}}, and most {{ill|komonjo|Q89298567|qid=Q89298567}} and {{ill|shinpō|Q11589458|qid=Q11589458}} were lost.

In May of {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}} 6, the current main hall was constructed by master carpenter Yokota Mokusaemon of {{ill|Takine, Fukushima|Q7678319|qid=Q7678319}}.

Under the design and supervision of Tsukamoto Yoshitaka, a consultant to the {{ill|Ministry of Education, Science, Sports and Culture|Q11080185|qid=Q11080185}}, the present {{ill|Heiden (Shinto)|Q3076699|qid=Q3076699}} and {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}} were completed in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 4.
